paragraphs: This checklist is used for self-questioning only and does not constitute a hiring standard, a competency rating, or an evaluation of furniture finishing quality or of a career. This page is written according to U.S. O*NET-SOC 51-7021.00 “Furniture Finishers” (the fixed index assigns this asset the Chinese name Furniture Finishers; the main objects are damaged, worn, or used furniture and new high-grade furniture, the goal is to shape surfaces to a specified color or finish, and the output is the repair and finishing results completed to specification together with process and material records). This occupation is mainly manual and spray work, involving wood and finishing materials and solvents and sanding dust and compressed air and flammable substances, and must be carried out according to institutional and local safety and occupational health and fire protection requirements; where old finish layers may contain lead and other hazardous substances and hazardous waste disposal is involved, disposal is carried out by qualified and authorized personnel and institutions according to local regulations.

Paper exercise｜Use the entry module to fully reconcile the F/V2 synthesized work orders, material consumption, samples, and missing-part data to compute area and budget, determine anomalies and items pending verification, and hand off; do not touch real furniture, solvents, dust, or spray equipment, and do not design or carry out safety processes on your own.

Observation signals｜O*NET88% continuous use of hands, 67% continuous standing, 93% daily common protection, 81% daily contaminants, 60% uncontrolled indoor, 46% precision extremely important / 30% very important, 51% errors fairly serious, 38% team extremely important. These are respondent options, not individual thresholds or exposure doses; use paper versions, calculations, and hand-off deliverables to observe the approach, and do not infer health tolerance.

Caution signals｜65% daily hazardous conditions; repetitive motion 21% continuous / 34% more than half; 49% limited freedom in tasks, 44% some decision freedom without supervision; 49% moderate competition; 33% daily deadline pressure, 40% at least weekly but not daily; 38% continuous contact, 68% never use the telephone, 75% regular schedule. The options do not equal accident rates, absence of overtime, or inevitable exposure for everyone. Specific protection, actual working hours, and qualifications are verified separately.

Exploration judgment｜Examining, repairing, sanding, selecting materials and mixing colors, finishing and decorating, and inspecting and communicating are the tasks of this occupation. First independently complete the four F/V2 paper deliverables and counterexamples, and judge whether you are willing to continue learning; the deliverables do not prove real craft, safety, or health competence, and real operations require applicable training, facilities, and authorization.

Direct answer｜The work of furniture finishers can be broadly divided into three categories. First, repair and surface preparation: examine furniture to determine the degree of damage or deterioration and decide on the best repair or restoration approach; fill and level cracks or depressions and remove marks and blemishes and repair broken parts with plastic or wood putty and glue and nails and screws; use hand tools and stripping tools and sandpaper and steel wool and abrasives and solvents or dipping to remove old finish layers and damaged parts; sand and shape and finish surfaces with sandpaper and pumice and steel wool and chisels and sanders and polishers and treat warping or stains to restore the original contours and original color; disassemble furniture for handling and mask parts that should not contact the finishing process or materials. Second, finishing and coloring and decorating: select finishing materials such as paint and stain and varnish and shellac or lacquer according to wood hardness and surface type and mix colors and color codes; apply finishing materials into the wood grain by brushing and spraying or hand rubbing; create a distressed effect with woodworking tools or abrasives, or treat the surface before staining to highlight highlights and shading; restore old pieces or decorate new ones with stenciling and gilding and embossing and branding and painted patterns or borders; finish metal surfaces by spray gun or electrostatic means and simulate wood grain with wood-grain ink; restore the natural color of wood with bleach; refurbish and replace upholstery and remove excess solvent. Third, inspection and collaboration and recording: communicate with customers to determine furniture color or finish; recommend wood and color and finish and furniture style based on knowledge of wood and fashion and styles; make specified designs according to drawings; inspect finish and surface quality and deliver; record materials and color codes and batches and processes and anomalies. The three categories of work link in cycles: examine and assess damage — disassemble and remove old finish — repair and sand and shape — select materials and mix — finish and decorate — inspect and hand over and record.

O*NET occupational profile highlights｜The official scope of O*NET-SOC 51-7021.00 “Furniture Finishers” is: Shape, finish, and refinish damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to specified color or finish. Of the 22 tasks given in the occupational profile, 13 are core tasks: apply finishing materials such as paint and oil and stain and wax into the wood grain and coat with varnish or other sealers by brushing and spraying or hand rubbing; fill and level cracks or depressions and remove marks and blemishes and repair broken parts with plastic or wood putty and glue and nails and screws; sand and shape and finish surfaces with sandpaper and pumice and steel wool and chisels and sanders or polishers to prepare for finishing; remove fittings and mask parts that should not contact the finishing process or materials before finishing; remove old finish layers and damaged or deteriorated parts with hand tools and stripping tools and sandpaper and steel wool and abrasives and solvents or dipping; treat warped or stained surfaces to restore the original contours and original color; select suitable finishing materials such as paint and stain and varnish and shellac or lacquer according to factors such as wood hardness and surface type; mix finishing materials to obtain the desired color or shade; remove excess solvent with a cloth soaked in thinner; examine furniture to determine the degree of damage or deterioration and decide on the best repair or restoration approach; create a distressed surface with woodworking tools or abrasives before staining to form an antique appearance, or rub the surface to highlight highlights and shading; restore the original appearance of old pieces or decorate new ones with stenciling and gilding and embossing and branding and painted patterns or borders; disassemble furniture with hand tools to prepare for finishing. There are another 9 supplemental tasks: communicate with customers to determine furniture color or finish; recommend wood and color and finish and furniture style based on knowledge of wood products and fashion and styles; clean surfaces to prepare for finishing; make specified designs according to drawings; finish metal surfaces with a spray gun or other coating equipment or electrostatic means; replace or refurbish upholstery with nails and glue and softeners and solvents and stains or polishes; design and make and decorate an entire piece of furniture or specific parts such as drawers; apply wood-grain ink to metal parts to simulate a wood-grain finish; brush wood surfaces with bleach to restore the natural color.

entries: Examination and assessment｜Extent of damage and treatment approach｜Examine furniture to determine the degree of damage or deterioration and decide on the best repair or restoration approach, and communicate with customers to confirm the color or finish.

Finishing and preparation｜Disassembly and cleaning and old-finish removal｜Disassemble furniture with hand tools and clean surfaces; remove old finish layers and damaged parts with stripping tools and sandpaper and steel wool and abrasives and solvents or dipping, and mask parts that should not contact the finish.

Repair and shaping｜Filling and repair and sanding｜Fill cracks or depressions and remove marks and blemishes and repair broken parts with putty and glue and nails and screws; sand and shape with sandpaper and pumice and chisels and sanders and treat warping and stains to restore contours and original color.

Materials and mixing｜Selection and color mixing｜Select materials such as paint and stain and varnish and shellac or lacquer according to wood hardness and surface type and mix to obtain the desired color or shade; remove excess solvent and make specified designs according to drawings.

Finishing and decorating｜Application and distressing and printing｜Apply finishing materials into the wood grain by brushing and spraying or hand rubbing; create a distressed effect or highlight highlights and shading; restore or decorate with stenciling and gilding and embossing and branding and painted patterns or borders; and treat special surfaces with bleach or wood-grain ink.

Inspection and collaboration｜Quality and handover and records｜Inspect finish and surface quality and deliver; recommend wood and color and finish and style to customers; record materials and color codes and batches and processes and anomalies and report according to authorization.

In China, work involving exposure to occupational disease hazards is subject to verification of training, protection, and occupational health examinations under the Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases; in the U.S., the applicable 1910.107 spray finishing standard requires verifying ventilation and ignition source control according to the actual materials and facilities. Whether an old coating is hazardous and whether waste is hazardous must be identified and determined in accordance with the law, and lead content is not determined by smell or by the age of the furniture; customer-identifiable personal data is verified separately under PIPL, while a pure formula is not automatically personal information.

Boundary conclusion｜The core difference between this occupation and adjacent positions lies in “object and output”: this occupation takes furniture and wood products as its object and completes repair and finishing to a specified color or finish, with the output being repaired and finished furniture workpieces and material and process records; carpet installers and floor layers and floor sanders and finishers produce floor materials and floor leveling and surface treatment; tile and stone setters produce tile and stone installation; terrazzo workers and finishers produce terrazzo floor pouring and grinding and polishing; cabinetmakers and bench carpenters produce wooden components and cabinet fabrication and installation; furniture upholsterers produce upholstery and padding and fabric covering. The objects and outputs differ, and the authority for color matching and surface treatment and release and handover cannot be carried over across positions.

Core concept of adjacent positions｜Most positions in the same group and adjacent positions aim to “complete surface treatment and installation to specification and keep quality and safety controllable,” and the difference lies in the object handled and the output: some take furniture and wood product repair and finishing as their object, some take floor and wall material installation and surface treatment as their object, some take wooden components and furniture structure fabrication as their object, and some take upholstery and fabric covering as their object.

Core purpose of this occupation｜Taking customer requirements and workpiece examination results as the object, and within the scope of safety and occupational health and fire protection and institutional authorization, turn furniture finishing into executable repair and finishing results and verifiable records: examination and assessment, disassembly and old-finish removal, repair and sanding, material selection and mixing, finishing and decorating, inspection and handover, so that repair and finishing quality is measurable and conforms to the specified color or finish.

Basis for adjacent objects｜Carpet base installation; 47-2042 resilient and sound-absorbing decorative floor covering blocks, strips, and sheets (excluding carpet, wood flooring, and hard tile); floor sanding and finishing; masonry and stone setting and terrazzo pouring; cabinet wooden components and upholstery covering. Specific drawings, materials, and processes are verified per position and are not automatically mutually recognized.

Main object and basis of this occupation｜The objects are damaged and worn or used furniture and new high-grade furniture, finishing materials and solvents and putty and abrasives, and color code and batch and process records, based on the customer-specified color or finish, material and workpiece examination results, and safety and occupational health and fire protection and hazardous waste and recordkeeping requirements.

Occupational profile｜This occupation shapes, finishes, and refinishes damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to a specified color or finish: examine furniture to determine the extent of damage and decide on the repair approach; disassemble and clean and use hand tools and stripping tools and sandpaper and abrasives and solvents or dipping to remove old finish layers and damaged parts; fill cracks and depressions and repair broken parts with putty and glue and nails and screws; sand and shape with sandpaper and pumice and chisels and sanders and treat warping and stains; select and mix materials such as paint and stain and varnish and shellac or lacquer according to wood hardness and surface type; apply by brushing and spraying or hand rubbing and distress and highlight light and dark; restore or decorate with stenciling and gilding and embossing and branding and painted patterns; refurbish and replace upholstery and treat special surfaces with bleach or wood-grain ink; communicate with customers to determine color or finish and recommend wood and style; inspect surface quality and deliver and record. Common employers include furniture manufacturing and wood products companies, furniture repair and refinishing workshops, custom and high-grade furniture makers, and building decoration and repair service providers; the work is characterized by long periods of standing and manual and repetitive motions, exposure to dust and solvents and spray, and wearing protective equipment, and the consequences of error are fairly serious; the authority and qualifications for handling old finish layers that may contain lead and other hazardous substances and flammable solvents and hazardous waste disposal are determined by qualified or authorized personnel and institutions and local regulations. Official definition text: Shape, finish, and refinish damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to specified color or finish.

Adjacent processes｜Carpet cutting and installation; 47-2042 covering material cutting and bonding and flattening and edging; floor sanding and seam filling and finishing; masonry leveling and setting and pointing; terrazzo pouring and grinding; cabinet fabrication and assembly; upholstery cutting and covering.

Core processes of this occupation｜Workpiece examination and damage assessment and confirmation of customer requirements; disassembly and cleaning and old-finish removal; repair of cracks and breakage and warping and stains; selection and mixing of materials and color codes according to wood and surface condition; application and coloring and distressing and decorating; surface quality inspection and handover and recording and anomaly reporting; each step must leave a trace according to the customer-specified effect and institutional procedures and be reviewable by the foreman and the quality and safety departments.

Main outputs of adjacent positions｜Carpet installers and floor layers produce installed floors and edging; floor sanders and finishers produce sanded and finished floors; tile and stone setters produce installed and pointed tile and stone surfaces; terrazzo workers and finishers produce poured and ground and polished terrazzo surfaces; cabinetmakers and bench carpenters produce wooden cabinets and components; furniture upholsterers produce covered upholstered furniture.

Main outputs of this occupation｜Repaired and finished furniture workpieces meeting the specified color or finish; material and color code and batch and mixing records; repair and sanding and shaping records; application and distressing and decorating process records; surface quality inspection and handover records; rework and anomaly and pending-item records.

Responsibility holders for adjacent positions｜Responsibility for positions in the same group and adjacent positions is usually defined by the affiliated institution and process and safety and quality standards and regulatory rules, and the objects of responsibility are mostly the institution and project quality and work safety and customers and the public.

This occupation may, within the scope of the position, select materials, mix colors, repair, and inspect; process changes, handover, hazard identification, and accident handling are verified according to actual duties and statutory conditions and unit authorization, and are not uniformly excluded from the individual or uniformly decided by the competent authority.

Adjacent positions may involve concurrent duties; material substitution, acceptance, and hazardous work authority are verified according to actual duties and statutory qualifications, are not automatically mutually recognized because of adjacency, and are not uniformly without judgment.

Statutory qualifications, training, and unit authorization in China are verified separately; whether special operations are involved must be based on the actual operations catalog and project, and the same certificate cannot be inferred for everyone from the names of furniture spray painting, hazardous chemicals, or hazardous waste. Unit authorization does not replace statutory certificates, and a U.S. occupation code does not confer Chinese qualifications. Equipment and material operation, process changes, and handover are verified according to the specific work order procedures.

Conclusion boundaries for adjacent positions｜Conclusions for positions in the same group and adjacent positions are mostly limited to the level of this process and this workpiece and this batch, and usually do not constitute a final determination of project quality and material safety and compliance; the application of conclusions across trades and institutions and jurisdictions has scope limitations.

Conclusion boundary｜Original workpiece examination, samples, material batches, and inspection follow actual records, and assumptions and estimates are listed separately; process changes, rework, and handover are verified according to the specific position's authorization, suspected hazards are reported according to the plan, and they are not uniformly referred to the competent authority.

Pre-employment verification notes｜The following six items are used to verify one by one before applying and onboarding, to avoid inferring actual duties and authorization from a job title or promotional language; verification results should be based on written recruitment information, employment contracts, job descriptions, and institutional policies, and should be continuously confirmed after onboarding. This page lists verification directions only and does not constitute a formal conditions list for any institution.

Verification point notes｜Similar job titles can differ greatly in duties: some focus on hand sanding and repair, some on spray painting and color mixing, some on upholstery and refinishing, and some on assembly and packaging; different institutions and processes also have different requirements for the authority to change materials and formulas and to release and hand over work.

01 Actual duties of the position and authorization boundaries｜Verify whether the role truly involves examination and repair and sanding and material selection and mixing and application and quality inspection, or is mainly handling and cleaning or packaging assistance; verify the approval path for material and formula changes and workpiece release and rework and handover and anomaly handling, and how overreach and anomalies are suspended and escalated.

Verification point notes｜Sanding and stripping dust, finishing solvents, spray, flammable substances, and compressed air carry safety and occupational health and fire protection requirements, and old finish layers may contain lead and other hazardous substances, for which testing and stripping and disposal are governed by separate provisions.

02 Safety, occupational health, and fire protection requirements｜Verify whether the institution and the position require safety and occupational health training and position qualifications, whether dust and gas and chemical and anti-static protective equipment and ventilation and dust removal and detection are provided and their use enforced, whether there are procedures and emergency arrangements for the spray booth and the paint mixing room and hazardous chemicals and hazardous waste management, whether there are testing and isolation and disposal processes for hazardous substances in old finish layers, and whether there are drills and reporting paths for fire, deflagration, poisoning, and burns.

O*NET newly hired education questionnaire: 61% high school or equivalent, 36% below high school, 3% postsecondary certificate; this is not the education of all practitioners or Chinese hiring stratification; Zone1—2 is a grouping preparation description, and the BLS typical entry for this occupation is high school, no related experience, short-term OJT, which does not equal a fixed individual proficiency duration.

03 Education, training, and qualification requirements｜Verify whether high school or equivalent education and related vocational training are required, whether training in repair and finishing and color mixing and spraying and safety and occupational health is provided, whether position qualifications or on-the-job experience in spraying and hazardous chemicals and confined spaces are required, and the specialized authorization requirements for handling hazardous substances in old finish layers and hazardous waste disposal.

Insufficient evidence: this round did not obtain precise national, city, and employment-type wages and employment for this occupation in China; industry averages are background only, a bounded search does not prove the statistic does not exist, and U.S. or industry values are not used as substitutes. Editorial verification: confirm in writing the working hours, whether overtime and piece rates apply, bonuses and allowances and compensatory leave; a 75% regular schedule does not prove a uniform peak season or income composition.

04 Pay, working hours, and contract terms｜Verify the composition of the offered pay (base wage, piece rate or performance pay and overtime or compensatory leave, provision of protective and labor protection supplies), working hours and peak-season scheduling and overtime arrangements, probation period and assessment terms, and whether allowances and medical examinations for hazardous environments and special working hours are involved.

Verification point notes｜The interface relationships with the foreman and the color mixing and spray painting and sanding and upholstery processes and with customers and the quality and safety departments determine the responsibility boundaries for material and formula changes and workpiece flow and release and handover, and must be clarified in advance.

05 Interface authority with the foreman and processes and customers and the safety department｜Verify the division of labor and handover method with the foreman and the preceding and following processes, the material and color code confirmation process with color mixing and spray painting and sanding personnel, the interface with customers for color and effect confirmation and changes and acceptance, the inspection and rectification and accident reporting paths with the quality and safety departments, and the handover paths for material changes and rework and anomaly handling.

Verification point notes｜The traceability and documentation requirements for materials and color codes and batches and processes and inspection and rework and anomaly records determine how quality is defined and how customer disputes are handled, and the version and revision and archiving and access specifications must be clarified in advance.

06 Records, data, and traceability requirements｜Verify the version and revision and archiving specifications and retention periods and access permissions for customer requirements and color and effect confirmation and change records, workpiece examination and damage assessment and treatment method records, material and color code and batch and mixing and construction process records, surface quality inspection and handover and acceptance records, and rework and anomaly and pending-item records; the approval requirements for the use and external provision of customer information and process formulas and color matching data; and the obligation to provide evidence and cooperate during quality traceability, accident investigation, and regulatory inspection.

Preface｜The following comparison is organized in four columns: “career direction — core work and output — key differences — what choice it suits better.” Furniture finishing and floor material installation and surface treatment often connect within the same carpentry and decoration chain, but connection does not mean they can substitute for each other; when choosing across directions, materials, tools, processes, and authorization requirements must be learned anew.

Focus of difference｜This occupation shapes and finishes damaged or newly made high-grade furniture, including metal surface and upholstery supplemental tasks; the five floor directions have different objects and processes, but specific concurrent duties are verified per position, and qualifications or wages are not inferred from task proximity.

Better suited to people willing to stand for long periods doing manual work in an environment with dust and solvent odors, who are patient with color and surface detail, and who can repeatedly verify and rework to the customer-specified effect.

This occupation: Furniture Finishers

Key difference: carpet installers produce carpet material cutting and installation and edging and base preparation, and their work object is the floor; this occupation takes furniture and wood products as its object, focuses on wood surfaces and color matching and finishing effects, and usually does not take on floor installation duties.

Better suited to people willing to take responsibility for floor base preparation and material cutting and installation and edging; this occupation leans more toward furniture repair and surface finishing and color matching.

Better suited to people willing to take responsibility for tile and stone surface measurement and layout and installation and pointing; this occupation leans more toward furniture repair and surface finishing.

Tile and Stone Setters

Key difference: terrazzo workers and finishers produce terrazzo batching and pouring and grinding and polishing, belonging to on-site pouring and grinding processes; this occupation takes existing furniture workpieces as its object and focuses on repair and finishing, and it usually does not take on on-site pouring duties.

Better suited to people willing to take responsibility for on-site batching and pouring and grinding and polishing and curing; this occupation leans more toward furniture repair and color matching and finishing.

Core work and output: base preparation and divider strip installation, batching and pouring and compacting and curing, grinding and grout filling and polishing and cleaning; the output is a poured and ground and polished terrazzo surface.
Terrazzo Workers and Finishers

values: F/V2 is entirely synthesized paper data, and actual operation based on it is prohibited. Fictional tabletop A is 1.2 m long and 0.6 m wide, counting only the single-side rectangular area; B is 0.8 m long and 0.5 m wide, counting only the single side. The original work order is V1 color K1, and the latest is V2 color K2 and replaces V1. Material M is an abstract budget unit with a coverage rate of 0.2 L/m² (purely a problem setting, not a coating product parameter); the budget adds 10% loss, and the unit price is 100 CNY/L; the manual paper budget is 30 CNY per piece for two pieces, excluding tax and logistics and other costs.

Problem setting: three AND conditions for compliance — the color code equals V2's K2, the number of defects ≤1, and the material batch record is complete — only then is it compliant on paper; a known color or defect mismatch takes priority as an anomaly, and if there is no mismatch but the batch is missing it is pending verification. In the synthesized check, A has color K1 / defects 0 / complete batch, and B has color K2 / defects 1 / missing batch. Draft D1 writes the total area as 1.22 m², the material cost as 26.40 CNY, and the total budget as 86.40 CNY; the above must be independently recalculated, and inputs cannot be back-derived from an incorrect total.
Paper or spreadsheet, calculator, timer; first independently list the inputs and units and then check the reference answer, and do not take real customers, furniture, or materials.

90 minutes: 15 verify version / 15 area / 20 quantity and price / 15 three conditions / 15 handover / 10 counterexample = 90; deliver the four items: input version table, area budget table, check condition table, and handover summary.

Reference: A area 1.2×0.6=0.72 m², B0.8×0.5=0.40 m², total 1.12 m²; theoretical M quantity 1.12×0.2=0.224 L, plus 10% is 0.2464 L=246.4 mL, material 24.64 CNY, labor 60 CNY, total 84.64 CNY. D1 area is 0.10 m² more, and material and total budget are each 1.76 CNY more; the 10% is added to the base amount rather than dividing by 0.9. A color K1 does not match V2 → anomaly, and even with 0 defects and a complete batch it still does not comply; B has 1 defect including the endpoint but the batch is missing → pending verification, and release cannot be inferred.

Keep the original input and the D1 error, and in revision D2 list each formula, unit, and reason for change; unknowns are not filled in as measured, and paper compliance does not constitute real-world quality release.

Counterexample 1: using V1 would misjudge A's K1; counterexample 2: assuming B adds a synthesized batch number and is marked as a new version, only then do its three conditions comply on paper, while A is still an anomaly.

Counterexample 3: only changing A's color to K2 but adding synthesized defect 2 → still an anomaly; if B's defects are changed to 2, the known anomaly takes priority over the pending batch. The color code is not a physical color difference, and the defect count is not a real quality standard.
Independently back-calculate the M budget quantity ÷1.1÷0.2=1.12 m², and total budget minus 60=24.64; synthesized revisions must be explicitly marked and must not pass as the original check.

Do not mix or spray, sand or strip, inspect a real spray booth, or design hazardous work procedures; the abstract quantities and defect thresholds are purely arithmetic problem settings, not product usage, medical, or safety parameters.

subject.name: Furniture Finishers
subject.summary: Furniture Finishers (O*NET-SOC 51-7021.00, Furniture Finishers) shape, finish, and refinish damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to a specified color or finish. The work includes examining furniture to determine the extent of damage and decide on the repair approach; disassembling and cleaning and using tools and sandpaper and abrasives and solvents or dipping to remove old finish layers and damaged parts; filling cracks and depressions and repairing broken parts with putty and glue and nails and screws; sanding and shaping with sandpaper and pumice and chisels and sanders and treating warping and stains; selecting and mixing materials such as paint and stain and varnish and shellac or lacquer according to wood hardness and surface type; applying by brushing and spraying or hand rubbing and distressing and highlighting light and dark; restoring or decorating with stenciling and gilding and embossing and branding and painted patterns; refurbishing and replacing upholstery and treating special surfaces with bleach or wood-grain ink; communicating with customers about color and finish and recommending wood and style; inspecting surface quality and delivering and recording. Official definition text: Shape, finish, and refinish damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to specified color or finish.
